Design complete. Root cause confirmed by profiling against the real 492MB DB: per-snapshot re-query over overlapping trailing windows is 59% of classify.py and 99% of lga_leadership.py; scipy/trough detection is 1%.

Decision: both range paths load once and slice, but with different shapes, because memory is the binding constraint on Viking:
- lga_leadership (SQL already aggregates to (date,LGA); full history = 106k rows / 30 MB) -> single full-range _load_lga_sums + date-bucketed searchsorted slicing. Parity provable: HAVING groups on (price_date, council), which no window can split.
- classify (raw per-station rows; full history = 2.23M rows / 540 MB resident, 881 MB peak -> would OOM Viking) -> one ORDER BY price_date scan feeding a 45-day deque of per-day buckets, ~7 MB resident. Yield buckets, not flattened rows.
Single-snapshot paths (the daily daily-db-update.yml path) unchanged in both.

Prototyped both: windows byte-identical to current queries. Projected on a GHA runner: classify 471s -> ~90s, lga_leadership 1019s -> ~40s; the two steps 25min -> ~2min, seed-db.yml 46min -> ~23min (history.py's network-bound 16min becomes the bottleneck).

experiments/2026-08-21_tau_cadence/ (README + tau_sweep.csv + tau_sweep.png). 12 tau x 3 cadences off one paid walk-forward fit, 14 folds / 5 stations / seed 42 / 54 cols (54:1a6ec2d84a69), all 36 cells dry-free.

Best-tau-in-hindsight vs production tau=0.25: 7d +0.009, 2d +0.086, 1d +0.062 c/L. The 1d gain is 2% of that cadence's 2.97 c/L headroom. The hypothesis is directionally right and economically irrelevant - the optimum does climb 0.20/0.30/0.35 as the grid refines, and it is worth nothing.

Decisive line is the flip count (acceptance criterion 3), and it inverts the usual reading: at 1d, moving tau 0.25 -> 0.35 changes 422 buy/wait decisions for 0.062 c/L. The changes cancel. That is a real measurement of NO effect, not an underpowered measurement of a real one - much stronger than a small-flip-count null. At 7d the comparable move changes 8 decisions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Realised CPL vs tau at 1d, same folds/stations/seed/columns: DONE, plus 2d and 7d for contrast.
- Stated verdict: signal-content limit.
- Decision-flip count behind the sub-0.1 c/L deltas: DONE (422 / 132 / 8).
- If tau moves, re-lock recommendation: tau does NOT move. NO re-lock, docs/STATUS.md unchanged.

Method caveat recorded in the README: the sweep picks tau in hindsight, so a flat curve RULES OUT the operating point while a dip would only have upper-bounded a gain. The curve is flat, so the definitive half is the half that applies.

Untouched and much larger: cadence itself. The model is 1.85 c/L cheaper at 1d than 7d regardless of tau, but fills 2332 times vs 752 (9.9 L mean fill vs 28.8) - roughly 3x the servo visits, a cost CPL does not price. That remains a deliberate re-lock decision, not an experiment output.

Merged as 9b8d255 (PR #335). Draw count decoupled from arity: block_seed() is an unbounded, never-restarting seed supply (first 30 values the historical pool verbatim, so <=30-pick banks stay byte-identical) and candidate_sequence lays repeated laps over the column list, so n_draws is a free parameter at every gradeable arity — 20 draws now reachable at arity 1/2/3 where arity 3 could previously reach only 10. Root cause was measured, not assumed: reusing a source COLUMN across draws is near-free (batch1 placebo-pair |rho| median 0.038, max 0.218, against a screen tolerance of 0.6) while reusing a SEED is what destroys independence (max 0.971) — correlation lives in time alignment, and an identical rearrangement preserves two columns' alignment to each other. That collision was live and deterministic in batch1's committed ruler. Also closes fps-3jj.20.

Merged as 4544c7a (PR #336). Removed placebo.MAX_RULER_ARITY and the run_arity_above_cap refusal; source-column reuse is now PRICED into the threshold by placebo.effective_n_draws feeding family_wise_z_threshold, so a wider candidate gets a wider, harder bar instead of no verdict. docs/routines/generator.md says nothing about candidate arity — the owner's standing position, stated on fps-3jj.14 and again 2026-08-26, is that constraining candidate shape to suit the ruler distorts what is being measured.

The cap was ALSO an artefact of crude modelling, which is the part worth carrying: the exposure arithmetic charged two draws the FULL texture ICC for sharing even ONE source column. Two draws sharing 1 of 10 columns share about a tenth of their texture, not all of it. Binary charge put a 20-draw arity-10 bank at 2.4 effective draws; the shared-FRACTION charge puts it at 9.04, and the bar then degrades GENTLY at every width (1 col -0.152, 10 cols -0.171, 35 cols -0.287 c/L). That is exactly what fps-3jj.21 said the old design failed to do. The cap was solving a problem the modelling invented.

Verified on batch1's real frozen frame with shipped code: a 35-column per-LGA candidate — which fps-3jj.21 opened by noting could not have a band computed AT ALL — builds a 20-draw bank and grades at -0.287 c/L.

Three review rounds, each round's findings introduced by the previous round's fixes; none caught by tests (the suite was green throughout). Two real defects found: (a) the BATCH-level family-wise gate still took nominal draws while every per-run bar took effective, which violated an invariant — a best-of-N correction came out LOOSER (2.602) than the uncorrected single-candidate bar (3.118), only reachable by feeding the two paths different counts; now pinned as a grid invariant test. (b) bar_draw_count_shift_cpl_held had started absorbing the reuse effect it exists to separate from thinness; now computed on nominal draws with bar_reuse_shift_cpl_held emitted alongside, asserted to telescope.

Remaining bound: placebo.TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND = 0.391 is now the load-bearing input to EVERY bar rather than to one constant — a 95% upper limit from an ANOVA that could not resolve below 0.359 (point estimate ~0), deliberately pessimistic. fps-3jj.23 measures it directly and every bar tightens when it lands.
